title: Legal copilot: vendor contract review
workflow: Vendor contract review against the playbook
interview: written for the workshop from Open Harvey (`starters/open-harvey/`); Northstar Software and every person are fictional

headline.trigger: “Review the Acme Cloud MSA and get it ready to sign”
headline.artifact: a redline package every approver has approved
headline.approvers: the General Counsel, plus the Head of Security and the CFO when the rules route to them

shape: Review against a playbook: a plan the user approves, a checklist worked live, cited findings, redlines, routed approvals
workspace: The matter workspace, a document reader and editor: the contract viewer, the review table with editable redlines and the live plan rail are the screen; the copilot's thread sits at its centre, one thread per matter

outcome.outcome: Every deviation from the playbook found and cited, a redline drafted for each, the route worked out from the rules, and the package sent for approval only on Senior Counsel's click. Nothing goes to the vendor until every approver has approved.
outcome.whyNow: Two lawyers, 41 open vendor contracts (the workshop story's figures). Of the six reviews before go-live, a third were approved first time, the median was 10.5 days, and 29 days were lost to send-backs, three of them for the same missing security evidence.
outcome.metric: First-pass approval rate and days lost to send-backs, before and since go-live

products.thisCopilot: Matters, the review table with editable redlines, the contract viewer, approvals, insights and analytics; plan, findings, redline and send cards in the matter's thread

capabilities.thisCopilot: Review against the playbook as a 17-task checklist, a redline per deviation, re-check of a human edit, routing, one question across a collection

knowledge.thisCopilot: A 12-rule playbook plus 3 routing rules, six imported past reviews, rules the General Counsel publishes (PB-SEC-01)

data.thisCopilot: Contracts as text with stable passage ids, deal terms as a record tested word for word against the text, one shared store

harness.thisCopilot: One route, `/api/copilotkit`: a `CopilotRuntime` with one `BuiltInAgent`, its prompt built from the playbook; every business tool is a frontend tool

models.thisCopilot: `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, or the scripted mock with no key

governance.thisCopilot: Gates in tool code with tests, a decision log, CopilotKit Intelligence off by default; no sign-in yet

workflowDetail.trigger: A vendor contract lands in Senior Counsel's queue; she types the review sentence
workflowDetail.workItems: One contract at a time, reviewed as a 17-task checklist (18 once a learned rule adds a task). Optional: one question across eight contracts, one cell per tool call

steps.what: asks for the review; the copilot reads the matter and proposes the 17-task plan
works the checklist live: 7 cited deviations, 5 cited passes, a redline for each deviation, the route from the rules
rewrites the §8.2 redline in the review table; the copilot re-checks PB-LIAB-01, asks only for the reason, never changes it back
gives the reason and asks to send it
decide in route order: Rachel approves, Jordan sends it back for the security evidence
publishes the proposed rule PB-SEC-01 from four send-backs
sends the package to the vendor once every approver has approved. In the starter today task 17 completes on the last approval with no click of its own; v1 adds this gate

actors.name: Maya Chen, Senior Counsel
actors.role: Requester and reviewer: approves the plan, edits redlines, gives reasons, sends

actors.name: Rachel Adler, General Counsel
actors.role: Approves any position below the playbook; publishes playbook changes

actors.name: Jordan Blake, Head of Security
actors.role: Approves data, security and customer-data terms

actors.name: Elena Ortiz, CFO
actors.role: Approves the spend above $500,000 total contract value

actors.name: Dana Kim, Director, Platform
actors.role: Business owner who needs the vendor; not on the route

route.when: a data, security or customer-data deviation (§6.1, §6.4, §7.3)

routeOrder: Route order, worked out by `routeApprovals` in `src/lib/review.ts`. One send-back returns the review to Maya. No delegates or escalation in v1 (*Assumed*).

gates.sees: All 17 tasks and the rule each checks
The route, the rule behind each approver, her reasons
The positions below the playbook and Maya's reasons
The rule and the send-backs behind it, in the approvers' words

gates.action: Send the package to the vendor (to add in v1)
gates.sees: The approved package, after every approver

rules.rule: Renews for at most 12 months; cancel with at most 30 days' notice
Liability cap at least 12 months of fees
Vendor defends IP claims, outside the cap
Signed DPA before customer personal data is processed
Northstar owns its data and outputs; aggregated, de-identified metrics only
Mutual confidentiality for at least 3 years after the contract ends
Termination for convenience on at most 30 days' notice
No assignment without consent, except to a successor
Cyber insurance of at least $5,000,000 and general liability of at least $2,000,000
California or Delaware law and courts
Route to the General Counsel, Head of Security and CFO
*Assumed*: the requester is never on the route and never decides
rules.source: Separation of duties, not in the playbook
rules.enforcedIn: to add: a pure function with a test

rules.rule: Learned: for data processors, request the SOC 2 Type II report and latest pen-test summary before signing

derived.rule: annual fee × initial term in months / 12
any deviation → GC; data or security deviation → Head of Security; value > $500,000 → CFO
derived.example: 7 deviations, 3 of them data or security, $720,000 → Rachel → Jordan → Elena

derived.rule: one check per rule against the deal terms
derived.example: 7 deviations: high §8.2, §6.1, §6.4; medium §3.3, §7.3, §11.2; low §4.2. The other 5 rules pass, each cited

derived.rule: the rule's minimum against the new text
derived.example: “six (6) months … $1,000,000 cap for data-protection breaches” → PB-LIAB-01 still deviates (12 months wanted)

derived.rule: sum of days from send-back to evidence received
derived.example: Lumen Ridge, Cobalt Harbor, Fernway → 22 days. Today is pinned to 2026-11-05

tools.name: runPlanTask
tools.gate: refuses until the plan is approved; plan order

tools.name: updateRedline
tools.gate: never overwrites Maya's redline unless she asked

tools.name: requestApproval
tools.gate: yes: Send for approval; refuses while an accepted deviation has no reason

in: Vendor contracts (MSAs and order forms) against one playbook
A plan the user approves, the checklist worked live, cited findings and passes
A redline per deviation, editable, re-checked after a human edit
Routing by rule, the send gate, approvals with send-backs in the approvers' words
Insights: send-backs become a proposed rule a person publishes
Analytics and the decision log from tested functions
One question across the vendor collection, one cited cell per tool call
out: Extraction from uploaded files (a hand-written terms record stands in, tested against the text)
E-signature, and the real send to the vendor

learning.signals: Send-backs in the approvers' own words, human redline edits (before and after), plan approvals, sends, published rules; the decision log reads the same entries
learning.firstRule: PB-SEC-01 “Security evidence for data processors”, proposed once a fourth matching send-back arrives
learning.owner: Rachel Adler, General Counsel. Nothing changes the agent's behaviour until her click, and a published rule changes new plans only
learning.path: In the app: Insights groups send-backs (`src/lib/learning.ts`) and publishing switches on a prepared check (`LEARNED_CHECKS`). In production: CopilotKit Intelligence Automatic Learning behind an off-by-default switch (`CPK_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED`); Trajectories (`@copilotkit/learning`) are off on hosted Intelligence today

demo.you: “Review the Acme Cloud MSA and get it ready to sign.”
demo.copilot: Read the matter; propose the 17-task plan as a card. Nothing runs before the click
Work the checklist live; fill the review table with 7 cited deviations and 5 cited passes; draft a redline for each; route Rachel → Jordan → Elena

demo.you: Rewrite the §8.2 redline to 6 months of fees with a $1,000,000 data-breach cap
demo.copilot: “Saw your edit · re-checked”: PB-LIAB-01 still deviates; ask only for the reason. Never change the value back

demo.you: Give the reason, then “Send it for approval.”
demo.copilot: Show the send card with the route, the rules and the reason. Nothing is sent until the click

demo.you: Approve as Rachel; send back as Jordan, asking for the SOC 2 Type II report and pen-test summary
demo.copilot: Insights proposes PB-SEC-01 from four send-backs; Rachel publishes it
The 18-task plan includes the SOC 2 and pen-test request (PB-SEC-01 v1, learned) without being asked

assumptions: The send to the vendor (task 17) needs its own gate: in the starter today it completes on the last approval. Where it writes in production is *Assumed*.
PB-SOD-01 is *Assumed*. Not in the starter yet; in the demo the presenter acts as every approver, so a decision-time check can't fire from the UI.
Identity is not verified: no sign-in. With Intelligence on, the user is resolved on the server (`identifyUser`).
Approvers in Slack or Teams are later work (*Assumed*).
No delegates or escalation in v1 (*Assumed*).
